new_sources.note_on_84pct: The specific '84%' figure does not appear verbatim in the .txt version of the report; however, the World Bank blog (blogs.worldbank.org/en/transport/supporting-vietnam-s-economic-success-through-greener-cheaper-and-more-efficient-trucking) cites 'average fleet size of only 5 trucks' from this study, and a separate WB blog snippet references '84% of capacity in fleets under 10 trucks' attributed to this study. The underlying data (1,400+ driver survey, nationwide company survey) is this primary WB report. The 84% should be cited as deriving from this WB primary study with 'WB study (2019) as cited in WB transport blog (2024)' for full transparency.

claim_b_asean_median_under5.finding: No ASEAN-wide primary source found providing a regional 'median operator' fleet size. The World Bank Vietnam study confirms Vietnam national average ~5 trucks/company. The Krungsri Thailand data shows 91.2% of registered hauliers are small companies (DLT data). But no ASEAN Secretariat, ADB, or other multilateral source was found with an explicit 'ASEAN median under 5 trucks' figure. This claim extrapolates from country-level studies.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: Vietnam's truck operators average 5 trucks per company (World Bank 2019); Thailand's registered hauliers are 91.2% small businesses (Krungsri Research citing DLT 2024). Across SEA, extreme fleet fragmentation is structurally similar but an ASEAN-wide median has not been independently verified.
[ASSUMED-N]: ASEAN median trucking operator runs under 5 trucks — to validate: ADB or ASEAN Secretariat transport working paper with cross-country fleet-size survey

claim_b_asean_median_under5.reasoning: Vietnam and Thailand data are now primary-sourced. Narrowing to named countries avoids an unverifiable aggregate claim while preserving valid fragmentation narrative.
